content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be different from how you manage bookmarks today? What problem are you hoping it solves?

Honestly, right now my bookmarks are a mess. I save links in my browser and in a few different places, and then I can never find anything again. They pile up into these huge folders and I forget why I even saved half of them.

So what I'm hoping for is a proper home for all my links — one place where, when I paste in a web address, it actually saves it in a useful way. Ideally it would grab the page's title and a little description on its own, so I'm not staring at a wall of raw web addresses trying to remember what each one was.

The big thing is being able to find things again later. I'd love to organize them with my own labels, and to be able to search through them and actually get results. And I've got two kinds of links, really — stuff I want to read later, and stuff I've already dealt with. I'd like to keep those straight so my "to read" pile doesn't get buried.

That's the heart of it for me: save a link easily, have it look readable, and find it again when I need it.

content: If a page later changes its title or description—or becomes unavailable—should Link Home preserve the title, description, labels, and note already saved, without silently replacing your information?

Yes, absolutely — once I've saved something, that saved information is mine and I don't want it quietly changed out from under me. If a page later rewrites its title or description, or even goes away entirely, Link Home should hold on to what I've got: the title and description as they were when I saved (or as I edited them), and definitely my labels and my note. Those last two especially — I chose those labels and I wrote that note in my own words, so nothing on the outside web should ever touch them.

The thing I'd hate is opening my collection one day and finding a bookmark's description has silently become something different because the site changed, or worse, my note vanished because the page went down. That would make the whole collection feel untrustworthy. The whole point of saving a link is that I've captured it — my copy shouldn't drift just because the original did.

So: keep everything I've saved, and never silently replace my information. If anything, if the page does change and you can tell, I'd rather you just let me know and let me decide whether to update it — but the default must be "leave my saved details alone." That's what I'd expect.
